result.Method of Attack: Kernel driver loads in Windows kernel, injects embedded shellcode into a Local System 32-bit process, executes encrypted .NET payload; Backdoor functionality via HTTP listener on IIS URLs allowing command execution, file upload/download, and proxy functionality including RDP proxying; Persistence via registry keys and loading in Safe Boot, monitoring and restoring driver file if deleted
result.Impacted Systems: Windows systems, specifically IIS servers on Windows
result.Attack Vector: Loading unsigned kernel driver via vulnerable legitimate driver exploit; Shellcode injection into Local System 32-bit processes; Targeting IIS servers with crafted URLs; Likely distributed via targeted attacks possibly alongside Exchange server exploits
Indicators of Compromise: Registry keys under CurrentControlSet\Services\WinTapix and SafeBoot keys
HTTP backdoor URLs containing strings like 'wOxhuoSBgpGcnLQZxipa' and response 'UsEPTIkCRUwarKZfRnyjcG13DFA'
